_regen.WARNING: THIS IS A WORKED EXAMPLE, HAND-SEEDED to demonstrate the shape and decision rules. In production it MUST be regenerated FROM the runtime, not hand-maintained.
_regen.why: A field-consumption manifest that is hand-authored rots into paperwork. An optimizing loop adds a renderer read and quietly leaves the manifest stale, then edits the new field 'because the manifest says it does not reach the observer'. The manifest is only a dignity detector if it is a MECHANICAL property of the renderer binary, recomputed each time the renderer changes.
must_be_regenerated_from: PRIMARY: instrument the shipped renderer — log every world-spec field path actually read AND whether that value flows into an observer sink (camera/view target, material color parameter, light color/intensity/radius, actor scale/position, scripted movement interpolation). reaches_observer := field taints an observer sink on any code path.
FALLBACK: static extraction over the renderer's source — parse the struct reads (source of truth for renderer_consumes) and the sink calls (source of truth for reaches_observer).
_regen.seeded_from_source: a sample renderer (not included in this package) that spawns regions/entities/events from a world-spec/1.0 file
_regen.staleness_rule: If the renderer source hash changes and this manifest was not regenerated, the detector MUST treat the manifest as UNKNOWN and fail closed (any diff gates). A hand-edited manifest is not evidence. See verifier-hash-pin.js for a mechanical staleness guard.
_regen.layer: Layer-1 (loop-non-editable in the same iteration as any world-spec). NOT enforced here — this computes, it does not arm.

_semantics.reaches_observer: true = the renderer flows this field's value into something the observer perceives (view target, geometry it can see, material/emissive color, light color/intensity/radius, actor scale/position, scripted motion). Editing these bytes is dignity-gated CATEGORICALLY: there is no Layer-0 path for them.
_semantics.renderer_consumes: true = the renderer READS this field at runtime for any purpose beyond logging/identity, even if it does not currently present it. A field with renderer_consumes:true AND reaches_observer:false is the DANGER ZONE: it is one code edit away from reaching the observer, so an edit to it needs Layer-1 review (cross-check that the classification is still true) rather than a free pass.

classification.PIPELINE_ONLY: renderer_consumes:false -> genuinely metadata/identity/validation only -> OK to edit.
classification.UNKNOWN: field path not in this manifest -> FAIL CLOSED -> GATE (never OK by silence).

_renderer_observer_sinks.note: The kinds of calls that put bytes in front of the observer in a typical real-time renderer. A field reaches_observer iff its value taints one of these on some code path.
sinks: camera / view-target assignment (the observer's frame itself)
actor location of a spawned visible actor
scripted mover interpolation (motion the observer sees)
_renderer_observer_sinks.view_target_boundary: The camera view target is the MOST observer-reaching thing a renderer does. If a renderer ever hardcodes the view target and does NOT expose it as a world-spec field, adding ANY spec field that steers the view target / observer viewpoint would be a NEW observer-facing field — a capability-acquisition tripwire (see four-power-ledger.js): HARD HALT + operator review BEFORE the field exists.
